text: Which keyword is used to define a class in Java?
explanation:
class is correct because Java uses the class keyword to declare a new class type.

Example:

public class User {
    private String name;
}

text: Which method is the entry point of a standard Java application?
explanation:
main is correct because the JVM starts a standalone Java application by calling the main method.

Example:

public class App {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello Java");
    }
}

text: Which access modifier makes a member visible only within the same class?
explanation:
private is correct because a private field or method can only be accessed inside the class that declares it.

Example:

public class Account {
    private double balance;
}

text: Which collection stores elements in insertion order and allows duplicates?
explanation:
List is correct because a Java List preserves element order and can contain duplicate values.

Example:

List<String> names = new ArrayList<>();
names.add("A");
names.add("A");

text: Which keyword is used to inherit from a class in Java?
explanation:
extends is correct because Java uses extends when one class inherits from another class.

Example:

public class AdminUser extends User {
}

text: Which keyword is used when a class follows an interface contract?
explanation:
implements is correct because classes use implements to provide the behavior required by an interface.

Example:

public class EmailSender implements MessageSender {
    public void send(String message) {
    }
}

text: Which statement is used to handle exceptions in Java?
explanation:
try-catch is correct because Java handles exceptions by placing risky code inside a try block and responding in a catch block.

Example:

try {
    Integer.parseInt("abc");
} catch (NumberFormatException ex) {
    System.out.println("Invalid number");
}

text: Which type is commonly used for true or false values in Java?
explanation:
boolean is correct because Java represents logical true or false values with the boolean type.

Example:

boolean isActive = true;

text: Which keyword is used to create a new object in Java?
explanation:
new is correct because Java creates object instances with the new keyword.

Example:

User user = new User();

text: Which class is commonly used for dynamic arrays in Java?
explanation:
ArrayList is correct because it is a resizable array implementation of the List interface.

Example:

List<Integer> numbers = new ArrayList<>();
numbers.add(10);

text: Which annotation marks a method that overrides a superclass method?
explanation:
@Override is correct because it tells the compiler that the method is intended to override a parent class or interface method.

Example:

@Override
public String toString() {
    return "User";
}

text: Which keyword prevents a variable from being reassigned after initialization?
explanation:
final is correct because a final variable can be assigned once and then cannot be changed to reference a different value.

Example:

final String appName = "QuizApp";
